The program must output the position (index) of the value if it is found, or the message `Not found` if it is not in the array. [5]

You may use pseudocode or a high-level programming language.

markScheme.text: Takes the value to search for as input
Uses a loop that goes through the items of the array
Compares each item with the value being searched for
Outputs the position (index) when a match is found and stops searching
markScheme.guidance: Accept a flag variable, exit, or break.

markScheme.text: Outputs Not found only after every item has been checked without a match

question: Describe how a **merge sort** works. [6]

markScheme.text: The list is split into two halves
Each half is split again, repeatedly (divide)
markScheme.guidance: Accept: the list is divided in half until...

markScheme.text: ...until every sublist contains only one item
A list with one item is already sorted
Pairs of sublists are merged by comparing their first items and taking the smaller one each time
Merging is repeated until there is one sorted list

question:
A program asks the user to enter their age. The age must be a whole number from 13 to 19 inclusive.

(a) State **two** values that are boundary test data for this program. [2]

(b) State **one** example of erroneous test data for this program. [1]

markScheme.guidance: Accept 12 as a boundary value just outside the range.
Accept 20 as a boundary value just outside the range.

markScheme.text: (b) Any value that is not a whole number, such as a letter or word (e.g. "abc") or a decimal (e.g. 15.5)
markScheme.guidance: Do not accept a whole number that is outside the range (that is invalid, not erroneous).

question: Explain the difference between a **syntax error** and a **logic error**. Give an example of each. [4]

markScheme.text: Syntax error: the code breaks the rules (grammar) of the programming language, so the program will not run / be translated
Example of a syntax error, such as a missing bracket, a missing colon or a misspelt keyword
Logic error: the program runs but produces a wrong or unexpected result
Example of a logic error, such as using + instead of -, > instead of >=, or a loop that runs one time too few

question:
A website requires a password of at least 8 characters.

Write a program that asks the user to enter a password and keeps asking until the password is at least 8 characters long. When a valid password is entered the program outputs `Password accepted`. [5]

You may use pseudocode or a high-level programming language.

markScheme.text: Takes a password as input and stores it
Uses a condition-controlled loop (WHILE / DO UNTIL)
The loop condition is correct: repeats while the length is less than 8 (or stops when it is 8 or more)
markScheme.guidance: Accept .length or LEN().

markScheme.text: Asks for the password again inside the loop
Outputs Password accepted once, after a valid password has been entered

(a) ...so it is clear what the data / code is for
markScheme.guidance: Award for a correct reason linked to a way given.

markScheme.text: (a) Uses indentation and white space to show the structure of the code
